items.title: Kering's $3.9 Billion Quarter Shows Gucci Isn't Fixed Yet
items.summary: Glossy's business analysis of Kering's most recent quarterly results notes Gucci sales remain in decline on a comparable basis even as the pace of contraction narrows, with North America among the only regions to show positive momentum, driven by new product and stronger in-store execution. Frames the North American uptick as a bright spot within an otherwise fragile group-wide turnaround story, with China and Europe still weak.

items.title: Aryna Sabalenka Holds Court at Gucci's Fifth Avenue Flagship
items.summary: WWD covered Gucci ambassador Aryna Sabalenka's appearance at the brand's Fifth Avenue flagship for a live taping of Vogue's The Run-Through just before the US Open, discussing her engagement, wellness routine, and admiration for Demna's direction. Standard ambassador activation coverage; included here for context to the item below on the social backlash it triggered.

items.title: Sabalenka Slams Reporter Over US Open Off-Court Schedule Question
items.summary: Coverage of the fan and press backlash directed at Gucci ambassador Aryna Sabalenka, whose Gucci flagship appearance and other brand commitments were cited by a reporter and online commenters as possible distractions during her US Open title defense, prompting Sabalenka to publicly rebuke a journalist for the question. Illustrates a case where a Gucci ambassador tie-in became entangled in negative sports-fan sentiment rather than pure brand promotion.

items.title: All the Ways the $150 Million Gucci-Alpine Deal Changes Alpine's F1 Future
items.summary: Motorsport trade analysis revisiting Gucci's $150 million Alpine F1 title sponsorship (Gucci Racing from 2027), with continued fan skepticism about whether a struggling fashion house can credibly buy cultural relevance in racing versus genuinely earning it. Notes analyst framing that Gucci needs F1's fanbase more than F1 needs Gucci, given Gucci sales down over 20% in the trailing year.

items.title: "Gucci Is Struggling So It Gambled $150 Million That F1 Can Make It Cool Again"
items.summary: F1 fan-community-facing analysis framing the Gucci-Alpine deal explicitly around Gucci's commercial weakness, arguing the brand is using motorsport as a public image reset rather than a confident growth move. Reflects skeptical fan-forum sentiment toward luxury sponsorship money entering the sport, an angle distinct from Gucci's own promotional framing of the partnership.

items.title: Gucci Customer Reviews Cite Quality and Service Complaints
items.summary: Ongoing crowd-sourced review thread where US consumers describe declining craftsmanship (stitching failures, zipper breakage, tarnishing hardware after light use) and unresponsive customer service and repair handling. Recent entries reiterate a persistent 'paying for the logo, not the quality' criticism and dissatisfaction with pricing versus perceived value, a running negative undercurrent independent of Gucci's own marketing narrative.

items.title: PurseForum Thread: Unpopular Gucci Opinions
items.summary: Long-running enthusiast forum thread where members continue to post dissenting takes on Demna-era Gucci, ranging from complaints that recent releases feel derivative of the brand's Tom Ford and Michele eras to defenses of the new direction's boldness. Represents genuine handbag-collector community sentiment, more mixed and critical than official brand coverage.

items.title: The 'Gucci Morty' Meme Continues Circulating Across Platforms
items.summary: Recap coverage of the still-circulating 'Gucci Morty' internet meme (a Rick and Morty character edit dressed in Gucci apparel, originally posted mid-August), noting continued spread across Instagram, TikTok, X and Reddit through early September with tongue-in-cheek 'aura' framing. Organic, brand-unprompted virality rather than paid activation; original Instagram post passed 100,000 likes and a related X post drew roughly 15,000 likes and 2,300 reposts.

items.title: Can Gucci Racing Put This F1 Team Back on Track?
items.summary: Highsnobiety questions whether Gucci's F1 sponsorship can meaningfully revive the brand's cultural standing, citing skepticism among motorsport fans about livery aesthetics and doubts that a commercially struggling fashion house can credibly claim authenticity in racing culture. Balances brand-strategy optimism with pointed reader doubt.

items.title: Gucci Seemingly on Cusp of Turnaround
items.summary: Trade analysis assessing whether Gucci's improving but still-negative comparable sales trend, alongside North America's return to growth, represents the start of a genuine turnaround under Demna and CEO Francesca Bellettini, or merely a slower rate of decline. Notes analysts remain split, with some cautioning against over-reading two quarters of stabilization as proof of a durable recovery.

items.title: Gucci Resale Value Compared to Other Luxury Brands
items.summary: Resale-market analysis (drawing on secondhand marketplace data relevant to US resellers) showing core Gucci bags like the GG Marmont and Jackie 1961 retaining roughly 55-80% of retail value, with the Jackie showing the strongest multi-year appreciation. Presented as a neutral consumer-facing value guide rather than brand promotion; useful counterweight showing resale strength persists despite reported retail-sales softness.
